subject: FintechCo - Post-demo performance & SLO checklist
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@fintechco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: FintechCo - Post-demo performance & SLO checklist

Hi Alex / Sara —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture the key performance/SLO items we discussed and the next steps (MAP) so we can keep momentum toward your evaluation checklist. Attached is the SLO checklist spreadsheet with fields we filled during the call.

Quick summary / SLO asks from FintechCo:
- Latency: target p95 <= 250ms for single-turn generation (primary goal).
- Throughput: steady-state 200 req/s for the inference path we demoed.
- Concurrency: support up to 50 concurrent requests during peak windows; burst to 120 for short durations.
- Streaming: yes — progressive/partial responses required. First-byte target <= 200ms for streamed responses.
- Fallbacks: need automatic fallback to lower-cost model variant when capacity constrained; canary rollouts for model changes.

What we (Redwood) will validate next:
- Run a focused benchmark using a representative load profile you provide (synthetic load + sample prompt set).
- Validate streaming first-byte latency with your largest payloads and with KV cache enabled.
- Confirm achievable p95 at target throughput and recommend batching/quantization settings.

Next steps (MAP):
1) Alex/Sara: share a sample production load profile (CSV) and a set of 10 representative prompts by Mon 06/28.
2) Redwood (Aditya + Michael): schedule benchmark window and provide a test API key + short runbook (ETA by Wed 06/30).
3) Joint call to review benchmark results and decision criteria — propose Tue 06/29 10:00 AM PT.
4) Redwood to provide high-level cost estimate for the evaluated config by Wed 06/30.

Attachments: fintechco-slo-checklist.xlsx (contains the SLO table + notes).
HubSpot: HS-12345 | Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCDefGHIjkl7890

If that all looks right, please reply with the load profile and confirm the proposed Tue 06/29 time or suggest another.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara.patel@fintechco.com>
Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo - Post-demo performance & SLO checklist

Thanks Marissa — this is great and aligned with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:
- Current observed peak for our LLM path is ~180 qps (5m rolling), p95 currently ~300ms (we're seeing tail at higher payloads).
- Streaming is critical for our UX (progressive rendering).
- Can you confirm whether Redwood supports canary traffic splits and automatic fallback to a quantized/cheaper model variant in the same endpoint? That would be key for our procurement.
- Also please include a ballpark monthly cost estimate for the target throughput/config so we can start internal exec-level sizing.

I'm attaching our anonymized production load sample (production-load.csv). We'll aim to get the 10 prompts to you by EOD Monday (06/28). Tue 06/29 10:00 AM PT works for Sara and me.

Thanks — Alex

Attachments: production-load.csv

Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo - Post-demo performance & SLO checklist

Alex — thanks for the quick reply and for sending the load file. We're aligned on the ask. Answers to your specific questions below and next actions: 

1) Canary + fallback: yes — Redwood supports traffic-split canaries with weighted routing and automated rollback/fallback. We can configure a primary model and a quantized (lower-cost) variant—our routing layer will failover to the variant if latency or error-rate thresholds are breached. We'll include the exact policy examples in the runbook.

2) Cost estimate: we'll provide a ballpark cost for the evaluated config after the benchmark run, but to give you a rough expectation up front: at 200 req/s steady with streaming and p95 targets in the 200–300ms range, customers typically see X units (we'll convert to a monthly $ estimate after we pick the batching/quantization settings). We'll include both hosted and dedicated sizing options.

3) Proposed benchmark & schedule: Aditya, can you confirm availability to run a 3-hour focused benchmark on Tue 06/29 10:00 AM PT? We'll validate p95, streaming first-byte, and concurrency scaling. Michael — we'll need your notes on kernel/quantization profiles to recommend config.

Attachments: redwood-bench-plan.pdf (bench steps + metrics we'll capture).

Thanks — looking forward.

Best,

Marissa
